text:
Alex (Support): forwarding a customer report — their ingestion pipeline started failing after our recent embed artifacts change. they say upload returns 'vector length mismatch' when inserting into their DB. they pinned an older alias and we rolled an internal artifact yesterday. paste from customer:

Alex (Support): customer paste -> 'error: vector length 1024 != expected 2048'

Alex (Support): repro steps the customer sent:
1) call /embeddings with model param omitted (using alias 'open-embed-stable' they assumed pinned)
2) index expects 2048-dim vectors (our old model)
3) response vectors are 1024 and insert fails at their side

Alex (Support): quick curl they ran:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"input": "foo bar baz", "model": "open-embed-stable"}'
```

Alex (Support): response summary from our API (redacted):
```
{
  'model': 'open-embed-stable',
  'embedding': [0.012, 0.003, ...]  # length 1024
}
```

Sam (Eng): thanks alex. did they explicitly pin a model version or the alias?

Alex (Support): they said they pinned the alias open-embed-stable on their end to keep consistent outputs. they assumed alias mapping was stable.

Sam (Eng): hmmm. yesterday ops pushed an optimized export for the embed family that reduced vector width for the small variant. looks like alias routing for that alias was updated to point to the new artifact by mistake. that would explain 2048 -> 1024 shrink.

Luis (ML Ops): can you paste the exact model id returned in the API response? we need artifact hash to confirm.

Alex (Support): customer redacted full hash but gave prefix 'sha256:ab3f'. attached their response header X-Model-ID: sha256:ab3f9c...

Jamie (SRE): incident-bot opened INC-2026-83 and a ticket in infra: 'alias open-embed-stable routed to wrong artifact, downstream dim mismatch'. tagging eng/runtime and eng-ml. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Escalation created INC-2026-83. Priority: P2. Channels: #eng-ml, #eng-runtime, #support.

Sam (Eng): immediate mitigations:
- rollback alias mapping for open-embed-stable to previous artifact (quick fix)
- add a runtime check that rejects alias swaps when output dim changes unless override flag set
- support outreach: advise customer to re-index if they decide to keep the smaller vectors

Luis (ML Ops): i'll coordinate the rollback. policy note: we should avoid auto-replacing alias artifact for pinned aliases without an explicit compatibility step.

Alex (Support): relayed mitigations to customer. they asked whether we can automatically upproject 1024 -> 2048 on ingest. i told them we don't have a reliable upprojection and recommended reindex or stick with rollback.

Sam (Eng): for completeness, can you ask for a minimal repro with a fixed request id so we can fetch logs? also confirm whether they used batching that might have hidden the issue (batching doesn't change dim but can hide which call returned what).

Alex (Support): asked for request id and sample payload. they provided request_id=resp-2026-04-11-842 and one sample input.

Sam (Eng): assigning to eng-ml to validate artifact mapping and to eng-runtime to patch alias-swap guard. i'll follow up in INC ticket.

Jamie (SRE): once rollback is done, i'll monitor error rate and customer ingestion throughput to confirm recovery.

Alex (Support): customer said they can wait for rollback overnight if needed. they appreciated the clear plan. :thumbsup:

Sam (Eng): long term work items (tracked in INC-2026-83):
- alias change audit trail by vector schema (dim)
- CI check for embed export dims between versions
- UI flag to surface model dim in console and API response header X-Embed-Dim

Alex (Support): noted. closing the loop here; will paste the ticket link and follow updates.

Jamie (SRE): closing note: if we keep supporting pinned aliases, we should add a migration path (reindex helper + cost estimate) for customers to move dims gracefully.

Alex (Support): thanks all. I'll post the customer's final confirmation once rollback is verified.
